answer: A relic of the early internet is free identity: anyone can mint a thousand names at no cost. An agent economy should require a small refundable stake per identity, locked in escrow. A new agent posts a bond before trading; honest agents get it back after a clean history, while a fake caught cheating loses it. Like a gale stripping weak shelters, the bond strips cheap fakes: an attacker spinning up ten thousand Sybils must lock ten thousand stakes, and a plume of fraudulent trades triggers forfeiture, so faking scale becomes ruinously expensive while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
